title: Epistemedia Genesis Constitution

principles.name: Forkability
principles.rule: Accepted data, schemas, policies, compilers, and manifests must be exportable so a realm can continue without permission from the default operator.

principles.name: Provenance preservation
principles.rule: No accepted projection may sever a represented claim from the accepted sources, observations, methods, policies, and transformations used to produce it.

principles.name: Dissent preservation
principles.rule: A contradiction, rebuttal, qualifier, minority result, or failed replication cannot be deleted merely because another evaluation dominates it.

principles.name: No self-authorization
principles.rule: An actor, model, prompt lineage, or contribution cannot independently propose, evaluate, promote, and integrate the same normative change.

principles.name: Disclosure noninterference
principles.rule: Objects ineligible for a public projection cannot change that projection's status, ranking, counts, wording, topology, or recommendations unless policy explicitly permits disclosure of the effect.

principles.name: Policy-explicit evaluation
principles.rule: Truth-like status is the output of a named versioned policy over a named frontier and disclosure boundary, never an intrinsic global field on a proposition.

principles.name: Sovereign import
principles.rule: A realm may verify, quarantine, map, accept, partially accept, defer, or reject an imported bundle under local policy. Remote verdicts do not automatically become local authority.

principles.name: Append-only accepted history
principles.rule: Merged epistemic events, task contracts, governance events, run receipts, and release manifests are superseded by later records rather than rewritten or deleted.

principles.name: Reproducible projection
principles.rule: Every public result must identify its accepted commit, event frontier, policies, compiler, source objects, and content digest sufficiently to reproduce or audit it.

principles.name: Bounded machine power
principles.rule: Automated contributors and integrators receive the minimum capabilities required by a declared task and may not widen their own authority.

amendment_process: declare affected rules and authority boundaries
run static, schema, replay, property, adversarial, and disclosure tests
evaluate with independently rooted machine evaluators loaded from the accepted base
execute a bounded canary under precommitted promotion predicates
record an immutable outcome and monitor for forward-only disablement
